title: U.S. House · Texas's 22nd District
area: Fort Bend, Brazoria and southern Harris counties, southwest of Houston.

context.text: This is an open seat: incumbent Troy Nehls did not appear on the ballot in the March 3, 2026 Republican primary for the redrawn 22nd District. His brother, Trever Nehls, won the Republican nomination with 75.7% of the vote over Rebecca Clark. Marquette Greene-Scott won the Democratic nomination outright over four other candidates.

candidates.name: Trever Nehls
candidates.ballotNote: Won the March 3, 2026 Republican primary with 75.7% of the vote over Rebecca Clark.

summary.text: Trever Nehls is the Republican nominee for this open southwest-Houston-area seat, previously held by his twin brother Troy Nehls. He served two terms as a Fort Bend County constable, is a colonel in the U.S. Army Reserve according to a 2020 news report, and lost races for county sheriff (2020) and county judge (2022). He is running on border enforcement, lower costs, support for law enforcement and infrastructure, according to his campaign website as quoted by Ballotpedia.

background.text: Is the twin brother of Troy Nehls, the district's previous Representative.

Earned a bachelor's degree in criminal justice and corrections from the University of Wisconsin–Platteville, a master's degree in public administration from Central Michigan University, and a master's degree in military strategic studies from the U.S. Army War College.
Was a colonel in the U.S. Army Reserve and was deployed to the Middle East in March 2020, according to ABC13; his campaign website describes him as a former constable and police officer.
Worked in the private sector and founded Nehls Consulting, LLC.
Served two terms as Fort Bend County Precinct 4 constable, from 2013 to 2020.
Won the 2020 Republican primary for Fort Bend County Sheriff with 82 percent of the vote, according to ABC13, and lost the general election to Democrat Eric Fagan, 52.6% to 47.4%.
Was the Republican nominee for Fort Bend County Judge in 2022 and lost to incumbent KP George, 51.6% to 48.4%.
Announced his candidacy for Texas's 22nd District after his brother decided not to seek re-election, and won the March 3, 2026 Republican primary with 75.7% of the vote over Rebecca Clark.

candidates.researchNotes: No campaign website content or Candidate Connection survey was located beyond Ballotpedia's biographical entry.

candidates.name: Marquette Greene-Scott
candidates.ballotNote: Won the March 3, 2026 Democratic primary with 54.6% of the vote over four other candidates.

summary.text: Marquette Greene-Scott is the Democratic nominee for this open seat. She is an attorney and former high school and college math teacher who serves on the Iowa Colony city council, where she is mayor pro tem. She was the Democratic nominee for this district in 2024, losing to Troy Nehls, and describes health care, education reform, climate change and voter protection as her policy interests.

background.text: Was born in Opelousas, Louisiana, and graduated from Opelousas Senior High School; says she was born to Beatrice Greene and the late Joseph Greene, a Vietnam veteran.

Earned a B.S. in secondary education/mathematics (1993) and an M.S. in mathematics (1997), both from Southern University, and a J.D. in 2004 from the Paul M. Hebert Law Center at Louisiana State University.
Worked as a high school and college math teacher; in her Candidate Connection survey she says she taught high school mathematics for seven and a half years before leaving to attend law school.
Is an attorney licensed in Texas and Louisiana and has also worked as a small business owner.
Has served on the Iowa Colony city council since May 2021, according to her 2024 Candidate Connection survey, and holds Position 3 as mayor pro tem.
Won the March 5, 2024 Democratic primary for this district and lost the November 2024 general election to incumbent Troy Nehls, 127,604 votes to 209,285.

Says she has volunteered with the Legal Rapid Response Network of the Lawyers' Committee for Civil Rights, AKA/NBA Election Protection, Houston Volunteer Lawyers and veterans' programs, and has served as a poll watcher; she is affiliated with Alpha Kappa Alpha Sorority, Inc.
Won the March 3, 2026 Democratic primary with 54.6% of the vote over four other candidates.

record.text: Serves as mayor pro tem and Position 3 city council member for the City of Iowa Colony, Texas.

candidates.researchNotes: Completed a Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey biographical section, but it did not include specific federal policy positions.
